question_text: A 33-year-old man presents to a physician with a 3-year history of gradually worsening tics and difficulty walking. He was last seen by the physician 5 years ago for anxiety and has been purchasing anti-anxiety medications from an internet website without a prescription because he cannot afford to pay for the office visits. Now he says his anxiety is somewhat controlled, but the motor difficulties are making it difficult for him to work and socialize. His family history is unknown because his parents died in an automobile accident when he was an infant. He grew up in foster care and was always a bright child. An MRI of the brain is ordered, which shows prominent atrophy of the caudate nucleus. Repeats of which of the following trinucleotides are most likely responsible for this patient’s disorder?
